data.title: Canada Retail Sales Rise 0.8% in September
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Retail sales in Canada rose for a second straight month in September as households spent more at gasoline stations.

Sales increased 0.8% from the previous month to a seasonally adjusted 75.31 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$52.51 billion, Statistics Canada said Friday.

The advance was slightly stronger than the data agency's preliminary estimate sales were up 0.7% for the month, following an upwardly revised 1.4% increase in August.

Core retail sales, which exclude gas stations and fuel vendors and motor vehicle and parts dealers, edged up 0.1% in September

Compared with a year earlier, overall sales were 7.5% higher.

The agency said an early tally of receipts indicate sales declined 1.5% in October. The figure was based on responses from 58.1% of the retailers surveyed and will be revised.

Write to Robb M. Stewart at robb.stewart@wsj.com

data.title: Kevin Egan Signals Push for Board Changes at SRX Global with 9.9% Stake
data.description:
Kevin Egan Signals Push for Board Changes at SRX Global with 9.9% Stake

Kevin Egan and Lee Kiewiet disclosed a combined 9.9% stake in SRX Global Inc., with Egan holding 7.9% and Kiewiet holding 2.0%. They filed their report on Nov. 20, 2026, one day after signing an agreement to coordinate their activities. They plan to engage with SRX Global’s board and management about ways to increase shareholder value, including possible board changes.

Investor Intent

Egan and Kiewiet say they intend to “engage constructively” with SRX Global’s board and management about ways to increase shareholder value. They specifically identified possible changes to the board’s composition, but did not name candidates or specify a particular change.

They also may propose changes to SRX Global’s capital allocation, ownership, board structure or operations, including a sale of the company or parts of it. They have not committed to any of those steps and describe them as possible future actions.

Investor's Background

Kevin Egan and Lee Kiewiet are U.S. citizens who describe their principal occupations as private investors. Egan bought his 1,605,070 shares with personal funds for about $5.97 million, including commissions. Kiewiet bought his 396,204 shares with personal funds for about $446,515, including commissions.

data.title: Canada Retail Sales Pull Back After 0.8% Rise in September — Update
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Canadian shoppers look to have reined in their spending in October after higher prices at the pump drove an increase in retail sales in the month before.

The value of retail trade in the country increased 0.8% in September from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 75.31 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$52.51 billion, Statistics Canada said Friday. That was a tick stronger than the 0.7% advance economists expected and followed upwardly revised growth of 1.4% in August.

An early look at receipts indicates sales in October dropped 1.5%, which would be the sharpest fall since February 2025.

That estimate suggests a soft start to the final quarter of 2026. Households have so far weathered heightened trade and economic uncertainty and the shock of elevated energy costs, but the job market has struggled in recent months and the central bank in late October raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years.

Statistics Canada offered no detail with its October estimate, which was based on the responses of roughly 58% of retailers surveyed and will be revised.

The data agency's survey for showed sales in September were up in five of the nine industry segments it tracks, led by trade at gasoline stations and fuel vendors. Stripping out fuel, sales edged up 0.1 for the month.

In volume terms, sales overall were up a modest 0.1% in September and 3.4% above the level a year earlier.

Total sales for the third quarter increased 1.2%, softening from the prior quarter's 2.2% growth, though the volume of trade for the latest quarter was up 1% versus a softer 0.4% in the second quarter.

Consumer spending has remained solid this year, and is expected by the Bank of Canada to help underpin a recovery in economic growth in 2027. Still, there are concerns households will cut back on outlays the longer energy costs remain elevated.

The Bank of Canada's focus on rising inflation risk prompted it to raise its policy interest rate. Annual inflation has been at, or above, the upper end of the bank's 1%-3% control range four months running, holding at 3.1% in October even as underlying measures of core inflation have remained more contained.

The September retail data showed gas and fuel sales were up a second month in a row, increasing 6.9% in nominal terms and 1.6% on a volume basis.

Sales at motor vehicle and parts dealers also rose a second consecutive month, climbing 0.2% from the prior month thanks to growth at new core dealers.

Core sales, which strips out both fuel and autos, nudged up 0.1% for the month with a boost from general merchandise stores. Canadians also spent more on clothing, accessories, luggage and leather goods and on health and personal care in September.

The sharpest fall came from food and beverage sales, driven by weakness at supermarkets and other grocery retailers.

The Bank of Canada projects the economy will slow in the final quarter of 2026 as the country adjusts to the latest U.S. tariffs, then recover next year. An estimate of industry accounts suggests gross domestic product contracted 0.1% between August and September after essentially no change the previous two months.

At the same time, employment in Canada has fallen three months running, driving the jobless rate in October to a six-month high of 6.7%.

Write to Robb M. Stewart at robb.stewart@wsj.com

data.title: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $62K: What Should You Do?
data.description:
Bitcoin price has fallen below $62,000 for the first time since early July, extending a brutal November selloff as institutional investors pull billions from the market. BTC touched $61,270 just now, before recovering slightly to trade around $61,700.

Bitcoin price has now lost more than 10% over seven days, with selling pressure spreading across equities, precious metals and other risk assets. Yesterday’s $582.2 million outflow from US spot Bitcoin ETFs added another blow, bringing November withdrawals close to $3.5 billion.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest single-day outflow since launching. The same session saw $727 million in crypto liquidations, with bullish traders absorbing most of the damage.

Institutional demand is weakening, leveraged buyers are being forced out, and the Federal Reserve’s increasingly hawkish outlook is making speculative assets less attractive.

Bitcoin is now approaching $60,000, a level that could determine if the correction finds a floor or develops into something uglier.Xrp (XRP)24h7d30d1yAll timeBitcoin ETF Exodus and $727M Liquidations Put Bulls on the Defensive

The ETF withdrawals are arguably the biggest concern for Bitcoin holders right now. Spot Bitcoin ETFs became an important source of institutional demand after launching in January 2024. Their buying helped absorb available supply and gave traditional investors a regulated route into the market.

That demand is now moving in the opposite direction. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $1.1 billion this week alone. November’s cumulative withdrawals have approached $3.5 billion.Bitcoin ETF Flows,

The pressure extends beyond ETFs. Rising Treasury yields and expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase in December have encouraged investors to reduce exposure to assets that offer no regular income.

Meanwhile, derivatives traders are taking heavy losses. CoinGlass data showed more than $700 million in liquidations across crypto markets over 24 hours. Long positions accounted for 86% of the total.

Bitcoin itself recorded nearly $202 million in liquidations, with bullish traders suffering the majority of forced closures.

This creates a difficult environment for buyers. Falling prices trigger liquidations, which create additional selling pressure and push prices lower. The reduction in open interest also suggests excessive leverage is being flushed from the market.

Discover: The Best Token PresalesBitcoin Price Prediction: $60K Breakdown or Relief Rally?

The immediate battle is around $60,000. Bitcoin needs to reclaim $62,000 and establish support above it before bulls can confidently argue that the latest breakdown was temporary.

There are three possible scenarios:

Scenario 1: Bitcoin loses $60K and heads toward $58K or $53K.BTC USD,

This is the bearish outcome. A decisive break below $60,000 could trigger another wave of stop-loss orders and leveraged liquidations.

The next downside area sits around $58,000, while more aggressive technical projections point toward $53,700.

The daily chart offers little encouragement for bulls. Bitcoin trades below its major moving averages, while bearish momentum continues to dominate. A sustained recovery in ETF flows would become increasingly important to prevent further deterioration.

Scenario 2: Bitcoin stabilizes between $60K and $62K.BTC USD,

This would give buyers time to absorb available supply without immediately reversing the entire November decline.

The liquidation wave has already removed considerable leverage from the market. If ETF withdrawals begin slowing, Bitcoin could establish a trading range before attempting another recovery.

But sideways trading alone would not confirm a bottom. Buyers need to demonstrate that they can defend support through multiple sessions.

Scenario 3: Bitcoin reclaims $62K and launches a relief rally.BTC USD,

A recovery above $62,000 would provide the first meaningful sign that sellers are losing control. A move toward $65,000 would then become possible, followed by resistance around $68,000.

Consistent ETF inflows, improving market sentiment, and a weaker dollar would strengthen this scenario. Without those developments, any rebound risks becoming another opportunity for sellers to exit.Should Bitcoin Holders Sell, Hold or Buy the Dip?

For existing holders, the decision depends heavily on their entry price, investment horizon, and exposure. Long-term holders who bought substantially below current prices have more room to withstand volatility. Selling simply because Bitcoin crossed a psychological threshold risks locking in profits or losses without knowing whether the broader investment thesis has changed.

However, investors holding leveraged positions face a different problem. Falling prices can trigger forced liquidations regardless of their long-term convictions. Reducing leverage and protecting available capital should take priority over waiting for a rebound.

For buyers, the temptation to buy the dip is understandable. Bitcoin is considerably cheaper than it was just weeks ago, but cheaper does not automatically mean undervalued.

Buying in stages rather than committing an entire allocation around $61,000 offers more flexibility if the market tests $58,000 or even $53,700.

Bitcoin price remains vulnerable to another leg down. The $60,000 level is no longer just a psychological milestone. It is where the next major battle between buyers and sellers.

data.title: Baltic index inches down on lower capesize, supramax vessel rates
data.description:
The Baltic Exchange's main sea freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, eased on Friday and logged a weekly fall, as declines in the capesize and supramax vessel segments overshadowed modest gains in the panamax category.

  • The main Baltic index , tracking capesize, panamax and supramax vessels' rates, edged lower by 3 points, or 0.1%, to 2,898 points

  • The index marked a 2.8% loss for the week

  • The capesize index (.BACI) fell by 12 points, or 0.3%, to 4,502 points, and posted a 4.6% weekly decline

  • Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-metric-ton cargoes including iron ore and coal, decreased by $114 to $37,324

  • Iron ore futures rose on Friday on hopes of year-end restocking by steel mills, though the contracts posted a weekly loss after breaking through previous lows earlier in the week amid weak demand and high port stocks

  • The panamax index (.BPNI) inched up by 8 points at 2,140 points, its highest level since October 22, and logged a weekly rise of 1%

  • Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, rose by $76 to $19,264

  • The supramax index (.BSIS), for smaller vessels, lost 4 points, or 0.2%, to 1,810 points, and posted a 1.4% weekly drop

data.title: Britain’s most realistic EU future looks Swiss
data.description:
By Jon Sindreu

Despite Brussels’ dislike for piecemeal deals, the UK-EU ‘Brexit reset’ is another step towards a Swiss-style web of agreements. That might boost GDP by half as much as full membership. But it may be the most plausible route to growth while trying to rejoin looks risky.

Full view will be published shortly.

Follow Jon Sindreu on X and LinkedIn.

CONTEXT NEWS

Britain and the European Union agreed on November 20 in a summit in Brussels to scrap the certificates and controls currently required for cross-border trade in animals, plants and related products, as well as to align both economies' emission trading schemes and to launch a youth experience programme that would allow 100,000 young Europeans to travel, work and study in the United Kingdom, and vice versa. Both parties still need to agree over the coming months on how much to lower tuition fees for EU students attending British universities.

About Provexis plc

AIM quoted Provexis is focused on the development, licensing and sales of its proprietary, scientifically-proven Fruitflow® heart-health functional food ingredient.

Fruitflow is a natural, breakthrough ingredient that helps with platelet aggregation. This helps promote normal blood flow and circulation, which in turn benefits cardiovascular health. Fruitflow helps the platelets to circulate freely and smoothly throughout your blood, without sticking to one another or to the blood vessels themselves. Freely flowing blood helps reduce stress on your cardiovascular system.

Fruitflow is a highly concentrated form of bioactives which is lycopene-free and contains over 30 known anti-platelet compounds. Published clinical studies have shown that Fruitflow works to maintain healthy blood flow in a similar way to 75mg aspirin but with a milder and reversible action; Fruitflow has a similar antiplatelet effect to a single dose of aspirin - but when taken daily, it has none of aspirin’s side effects.

The science behind Fruitflow has been validated by leading peer review publications and regulatory authorities. Fruitflow is the only natural antiplatelet to have a health claim approved by the European Food Safety Authority, stating that 150mg of Fruitflow ‘helps maintain normal platelet aggregation, which contributes to healthy blood flow’.

Fruitflow has a number of specific health benefits which have been reflected in separate patent filings for the use of Fruitflow in:

  • mitigating exercise-induced inflammation;
  • managing blood pressure;
  • protecting against the adverse effects of air pollution on the body’s cardiovascular system. Laboratory work has shown that Fruitflow can reduce the platelet activation caused by airborne particulate matter, such as that from diesel emissions, by approximately one third; and
  • conferring health benefits in modulating the gut microbiome of humans, to include a reduction in TMAO, following the completion of a successful human study which is further detailed here www.dsm-firmenich.com/en/businesses/health-nutrition-care/news/press-releases/2023-01-20-new-study-reveals-dsms-fruitflow-activates-gut-heart.html.

Provexis sells a high quality dietary supplement product containing Fruitflow and Omega-3 from its website www.fruitflowplus.com on a mail order basis. The product is also available to purchase from Amazon.co.uk.

Provexis has been working with BYHEALTH, a circa £2bn listed Chinese dietary supplement business, for more than ten years to support the planned launch of a number of Fruitflow based products in the Chinese market. Clinical studies conducted in China are typically required to obtain the necessary regulatory clearances in China, and a significant investment in eight separate Fruitflow studies has been undertaken at BYHEALTH’s expense. Completed studies have shown excellent results in use for Fruitflow, and they provide strong evidence for the efficacy of Fruitflow on platelet function.

The Chinese regulatory system for functional health food ingredients, such as Fruitflow, is governed by the State Administration for Market Regulation (the ‘SAMR’) and it is based on a defined list of permitted health function claims which brand owners are permitted to use on product labels.

In August 2023 the Company was delighted to report that BYHEALTH had submitted: i) the first application for a new permitted health function claim and ii) some related product registration applications.

The significance of these major developments for Fruitflow in China is further outlined here www.nutraingredients-asia.com/Article/2023/09/05/china-set-to-approve-new-function-claims-for-health-foods. BYHEALTH has noted that it has been working on the project since 2015, with ‘tens of millions of funds’ (RMB) invested by BYHEALTH in the research and development work.

Provexis was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Reading, Berkshire. Provexis’ shares are traded on the AIM market of the London Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol PXS.

data.title: C.H. Robinson Secures Up to $500 Million for RXO Acquisition Financing
data.description:
C.H. Robinson entered into a delayed-draw term loan agreement for up to $500 million to help finance its planned acquisition of RXO, with the loan due two years after funding. The company also amended its receivables financing arrangements, including extending a $750 million facility through November 17, 2028 and transferring the administrative agent role to Wells Fargo. Related documents include an amended performance guaranty and an amendment to the receivables sale agreement.

  • Reason: Help finance the RXO acquisition and related expenses

  • Agreement type: Seventh amendment to receivables purchase agreement
  • Counterparty: Bank of America and Wells Fargo
